headline: Indian markets are **closed today** (Tuesday) for Diwali-Balipratipada. The night brought clearly good news: US stocks jumped over 2%, Asia is rising and oil fell about 6%, so Wednesday's open looks set to start higher, but US inflation data tonight can still change that.

mood.label: Positive
mood.why: The dashboard scores +30 (mildly bullish) with 3 of 4 checks agreeing, and the night's news supports it; options are expensive and fear is rising, which keeps confidence at medium. Overnight data as of 08:47 IST.

key_points.text: NSE and BSE are shut today for Diwali-Balipratipada. Everything below is about **Wednesday's open**, and global markets have one more day to move before then.
Since India closed on Monday, the S&P 500 rose **2.3%**, Korea's Kospi is up 4.6%, Japan's Nikkei 1.7%, and Brent crude fell 5.7% to about $92. All of this is good for Indian stocks.
FIIs (foreign funds) bought **₹7,212 crore** of Indian shares on Monday, almost 2 times their normal daily amount. They have bought about ₹53,000 crore so far in November.
My call: the rally is more likely to **continue at Wednesday's open** than to reverse, with medium confidence. A hot US inflation number tonight is the main thing that could prove this wrong.
Nifty has climbed about 10% in eight sessions to 25,045, its highest close in over eight months. Domestic funds are selling into the rise, so the market is stretched and quick dips are possible.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought better news for India, and it supports Monday's small gain and the bigger rally before it.

points.text: US stocks had their best day since April: S&P 500 **+2.35%**, Nasdaq +2.74%. Reports say lower oil and a bounce after last week's tech sell-off drove it. US futures are up a little more (+0.1% to +0.3%).
Asia is following: Korea **+4.6%** and Japan +1.7% this morning, led by chip stocks. Hong Kong, China and Taiwan had no fresh figures in the data yet.

Brent crude is down **5.7%** since India closed, to about $91.8. Reuters-linked reports say this came after President Trump said he would hold off new strikes on Iran. India buys most of its oil, so cheaper oil helps.
US-listed Indian shares: HDFC Bank **+2.7%**, ICICI Bank +1.7%, India ETF +1.0%, which is good for banks. But Infosys and Wipro fell about 0.9%, so IT may lag.

The US 10-year bond rate (4.87%), the dollar and gold barely moved. I couldn't confirm a reliable current GIFT Nifty figure (the overnight indicator for India's open), so I can't give its exact signal.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a big up run, I think continuation at Wednesday's open is more likely than a pullback, with medium confidence.

points.text: For continuation: overnight news is positive across the board, FIIs are still buying in big amounts, and futures show **new buying** (price up with more open contracts on Monday).
FIIs still hold more bets on a fall than on a rise in index futures: only **27% long**, up from 10.6% a week ago. If they keep closing those bets, it adds fuel to the rise.

For a pause: Nifty is up about **10% in eight sessions**, and domestic funds sold ₹7,173 crore on Monday, almost exactly matching FII buying. Reports also say Nifty fell sharply during Monday before recovering.
India VIX (the fear gauge) is rising (**17.4**, higher than 79% of the past year) even as prices rise. That is unusual and means traders are paying more for protection.
What would prove me wrong: US core inflation above the 0.2% monthly forecast tonight, oil jumping back up, or Nifty closing below **25,000** on Wednesday.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The dashboard reads mildly bullish (+30 out of 100), with three of four checks agreeing.

points.text: Price trend: Nifty is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (23,374, 23,283 and **23,988**). The swing pattern is still read as a sideways range, so this step scores +1 of 2.

Futures: on Monday the price rose and open contracts rose **1.8%**, which the dashboard reads as new buying (+1.25). Over 5 sessions, contracts fell 14% as price rose, a sign that much of the rally came from bears closing their bets.
Option chain: sellers of put options (people betting Nifty won't fall below a level) added the most at **25,000** and 24,900. The dashboard reads this as bullish (+1.1).

Put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) slid from 1.40 to **1.23** in 5 sessions. The dashboard reads this as put sellers pulling back, a bearish sign (−1), and the one check that disagrees.
Volatility is **high** (79th percentile) and rising, so option prices are expensive. Big swings both ways are more likely than usual.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign funds are buying heavily while domestic funds take profits, and FIIs still have bets on a fall left to close.

points.text: FIIs bought **₹7,212 crore** net on Monday. Their normal daily flow over the last 20 days was about ₹3,750 crore, so this was a large day.
FII buying this month totals about **₹53,200 crore**. News reports say global investors are moving money out of AI-linked stocks abroad and into India, seen as a non-AI market with steady earnings.
Domestic funds (DIIs) sold **₹7,173 crore** on Monday and about ₹32,000 crore this month. They are selling into the rally, which could cap gains if FII buying slows.
FIIs remain net short **90,741** index-futures contracts, but they cut that by 9,675 on Monday. They are slowly turning less negative, not yet positive.
NSDL data for late October showed FIIs bought IT (**₹10,915 crore**) and telecom (₹11,065 crore) and sold FMCG, autos and oil & gas. This is older data and may not match this month's buying.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheaper oil and calmer markets help India, but a likely US rate hike is the main worry.

points.text: Brent crude is down about **12%** in a month. Cheaper oil lowers India's import bill and inflation and helps companies that use fuel, like airlines and paint makers.
The rupee has strengthened about **2.9%** against the dollar in a month (₹93.93 per dollar), and the US 10-year bond rate is down 0.36 points. Both make India more attractive to foreign money.

The data shows US 6-month bills pay 0.38 points more than the Fed's rate, which means markets expect the **Fed to raise rates**. Reports put the chance of a December hike at roughly 75–85%. Higher US rates can pull money out of India.
Nvidia fell about **4%** on Monday after its board began investigating CEO Jensen Huang over a relationship with an alleged foreign spy. It didn't stop the wider rally, but it adds risk to AI stocks.
The dashboard's overall global reading is **Tailwinds**: 4 factors help India, 2 hurt it.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Most Nifty 50 companies that reported this week showed strong profit growth.

points.text: Hindalco's profit rose **59%** and revenue 39% from last year. Reports disagree on whether the stock rose or fell after it, so I couldn't confirm the market's reaction.
Titan's profit more than doubled (**+114%**), and Bharti Airtel (+24%), ONGC (+47%) and Apollo Hospitals (+34%) also rated Strong on the dashboard's rule.
Tata Steel's profit grew **16%** on 11.5% higher revenue, an in-line result. I couldn't find reliable reporting on how the stock reacted.
The data shows M&M's figures as zero growth, which looks like a data problem, so I couldn't judge its result.
Next Nifty 50 results: **Eicher Motors**, Grasim and Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles on Friday, 13 November.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Two inflation reports this week, US tonight and India on Thursday, are the big tests for the rally.

points.text: **US inflation tonight (7 pm IST)**: forecasts are +0.3% for the month overall and +0.2% for core prices (excluding food and fuel). A higher number would raise the chance of a US rate hike and could undo some of the overnight gains.
**India's CPI inflation on Thursday, 12 November, 4 pm**: lower oil should help. A low number would support hopes for easier RBI policy at its 4 December meeting.
US producer prices on Friday, then the Nifty weekly expiry on **17 November** and the monthly expiry on 23 November, when options-related swings can get bigger.
If FII buying slows while domestic funds keep selling, the rally could stall. Watch whether FIIs stay net buyers on Wednesday.
The Fed's next decision lands around midnight IST on **10 December**, and markets expect a hike.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would break the biggest wall of call sellers and open more room up; a close below 25,000 would break the main put-seller floor, just 45 points under Monday's close, and suggest the rally is tiring.

watch.text: Fed Governor Waller speaks. Any hint of a December rate hike matters for foreign flows.
US inflation (CPI) for October. Core above 0.2% would be bad news for Wednesday's open.
Oil overnight: Brent staying near $92 or lower helps; a jump back toward $97 would hurt.
Wednesday open: does Nifty hold above 25,000, and do FIIs keep buying?
Nvidia and chip stocks in the US: a deeper AI sell-off has been pushing global money toward India.

bottom_line: Indian markets are closed today, and the night brought good news: strong US and Asian markets, much cheaper oil and gains in US-listed Indian banks. The dashboard is mildly bullish (+30, 3 of 4 checks agree), and heavy FII buying supports it, so a higher start on Wednesday looks more likely than a fall. Confidence is medium because Nifty has already run up about 10% in eight sessions, domestic funds are selling, and fear (VIX) is rising. The main risk is a hot US inflation number tonight, which would boost US rate-hike bets and could erase the overnight gains before India reopens.
